checks.name: steps_completed
checks.why: the controller must complete every step it asked for; a run that exits 0 having stepped zero times is the stale-libController signature, and it looks identical to a pass

checks.name: exit_code
checks.why: a clean exit is part of the rung

checks.name: finite_clock
checks.why: the simulated clock must advance by steps x dt

rows.title: empty world loads, steps, exits clean

checks.name: rest_z
checks.why: a box of half-height 0.100 m resting on a floor whose top is at z=0.500 m has its centre at z=0.600 m; contact compliance may sink it by up to g*tau^2 ~ 4 mm

checks.name: contact_penetration
checks.why: how far the box sank INTO the floor.  Failing this while rest_z passes means the contact is softer than the solver's own defaults imply -- a different claim from 'the body is on the wrong surface'

checks.name: z_drift
checks.why: a body at rest must stay at rest: peak-to-peak z over the settle window is zero for a body in equilibrium

checks.name: spawn_z
checks.why: the first pose the controller observes must be the pose the world authored (z=1.60 m)

checks.name: fall_interval
checks.why: free fall from rest at z=1.60 m: the interval between crossing z=1.20 m and z=0.60 m is sqrt(2(z0-z2)/g)-sqrt(2(z0-z1)/g); clock-shift invariant

checks.name: fall_time_abs
checks.why: absolute time from the controller's t=0 to first contact, sqrt(2d/g) for d=1.00 m; a shifted clock shows up here and NOT in fall_interval, which is how the two separate

checks.name: rest_z
checks.why: after the drop the box must come to rest at the same analytic height as rung 1

checks.name: omega_driven
checks.why: an unloaded velocity-controlled joint reaches its command exactly at steady state: no gravity torque about a vertical axis, no damping, no contact

checks.name: omega_zero
checks.why: commanding zero must PRODUCE zero -- the case a servo that silently ignores its input passes only by accident

checks.name: angle_travelled
checks.why: integral form of the same claim, read from the joint's own position sensor: theta = omega t

checks.name: distance
checks.why: d = omega r t for a wheel rolling without slip, measured over a window that starts after the spin-up transient

checks.name: wheel_omega
checks.why: the wheels must actually TURN at the commanded rate -- read from each wheel's own position sensor

checks.name: rolling_consistency
checks.why: v_body / (omega_wheel r) == 1.  THE anti-slide assertion: a chassis that slid the right distance on wheels that never turned passes 'distance' and fails only here

checks.name: roll_overrun
checks.why: max over the WHOLE run of (v_body/(omega_wheel r) - 1), clamped at 0.  A wheel can push a body at most omega r and slip only makes it slower, so any excess is unphysical.  This is the check a steady-state window cannot make

checks.name: ride_height
checks.why: the axle of a suspensionless rover on flat ground stays at floor_top + wheel_radius; a rover being launched, or one that has driven off the edge, breaks every other number in this rung while leaving them looking plausible

checks.name: lateral_drift
checks.why: a symmetric robot given identical wheel commands on flat ground travels straight

checks.name: range_static
checks.why: with the carrier parked at x=0.00 m the sensor sits at x=0.10 m and the wall's near face at x=3.00 m, so the ray is 2.90 m long -- pure geometry, no dynamics in it

checks.name: range_final
checks.why: after sweeping 2.00 m the same geometry gives 0.90 m.  THE READING MUST CHANGE: a sensor frozen at its t=0 value passes range_static and fails only here

checks.name: range_tracks
checks.why: max over the WHOLE run of |reading - (wall face - sensor x)|, the sensor read against the pose recorded on the same step.  A windowed check sees two instants; this sees every one, which is what a sensor that stops updating needs

checks.name: sweep_span
checks.why: the carrier's own peak-to-peak x.  It separates 'the sensor is frozen' from 'the scene is frozen' -- without it a world that never moved would be reported as a dead sensor

rows.title: distance sensor swept toward a wall

checks.name: stop_gap
checks.why: the rover stops when the sensor first reads below 0.50 m, and may then travel at most 29.3 mm further (3 steps of latency plus 3x the friction-limited braking distance v^2/2 mu g).  MEASURED FROM THE POSE, so a fabricated sensor cannot grade itself

checks.name: min_gap
checks.why: the SMALLEST gap over the whole run.  A rover that ran into the wall and rebounded to a plausible resting place passes stop_gap and fails only here -- the same shape as rung 4's roll_overrun, and the reason a final-state check is never enough

checks.name: trigger_reading
checks.why: the sensor value on the step the stop was commanded: it must be the threshold, reached from above within one step of travel.  Unmeasurable -- and therefore RED -- when the sensor never crossed the threshold at all

checks.name: sensor_agrees
checks.why: rung 5's claim under real locomotion: max over the whole run of |reading - (wall face - sensor x)|, with the sensor pose now produced by the wheels rather than written by the driver

checks.name: stop_creep
checks.why: peak-to-peak x over the last 1.0 s.  A stopped rover stays stopped; the tolerance is the same contact-compliance bound as a resting box

checks.name: wheel_stop
checks.why: the wheels themselves must be at zero, not merely the body: a chassis held still by friction while its wheels spin passes stop_creep and fails here

rows.title: drive forward, stop at a sensed threshold

checks.name: distance_worst
checks.why: worst relative error over the 5 robots of d_i vs omega_i r t, each judged against the distance it would travel ALONE over the 4.0 s window.  This IS the non-interference assertion: a robot perturbed by a neighbour misses its own solo target

checks.name: wheel_omega_worst
checks.why: worst relative error of any robot's mean wheel rate against ITS OWN command; five different commands, so a command that leaked between robots shows up here

checks.name: min_separation
checks.why: minimum over the WHOLE run of every robot pair's planar centre distance.  All five start abreast 1.5 m apart and travel at different speeds, so they can only separate: the minimum is the lane spacing, at t=0.  Asserted geometrically rather than as a contact count, because a contact read that returns nothing is indistinguishable from nothing touching

checks.name: lateral_worst
checks.why: worst |y - y_0| over every robot and every sample: each robot must stay in its own lane

checks.name: roll_overrun_worst
checks.why: rung 4's one-sided kinematic invariant, over the fleet and the whole run: no body may outrun its own wheels

checks.name: ride_worst
checks.why: worst axle deviation from floor_top + wheel_radius over every robot and every sample after the initial settle

rows.title: five robots, five commands, one floor

checks.name: part_rest_z
checks.why: before the fingers close, the payload rests where geometry says: table top 0.70 m plus half its 0.06 m edge.  It separates 'the grasp failed' from 'the scene was already wrong'

checks.name: carry_rel
checks.why: max over the WHOLE run of |r_payload - r_wrist|.  The wrist origin is AUTHORED at the payload's centre, so this expectation is an analytic zero rather than a value read from the run -- the payload tracks the gripper, or it does not

checks.name: lift_height
checks.why: payload centre while held at the target: rest height 0.73 m plus the commanded 0.15 m lift

checks.name: place_x
checks.why: the payload ends at the commanded target, 0.45 m from where it was picked up -- 8x its own edge, so a carry cannot be confused with a jiggle

checks.name: hold_clearance
checks.why: minimum over the whole carry of (payload underside - table top).  AIRBORNE, asserted over every sample of the carry rather than at the end of it, so a payload that touched down mid-traverse cannot be rescued by where it finished

checks.name: part_speed_max
checks.why: fastest the payload ever moves, read over 50 ms windows so sampling noise cannot set it.  The measured failure this guards is a pinch that EJECTED its part at 3.5 m/s and left it on the gripper's own wrist plate

rows.title: gripper lifts a payload off a table

checks.name: repeat_delta
checks.why: max over EVERY body, coordinate and sample of |a - b| for two runs of the identical scene from two fresh processes.  Identical inputs, identical code path, one machine and one build: anything but zero is state that leaked between runs or an ordering that is not reproducible.  Whole-run, so two runs that diverge at t=2 and reconverge by chance at t=8 still fail.  ! SCOPED TO THE PRECISION THE POSE READBACK CARRIES, which is MEASURED to be single: a cube authored at x=0.502 reads back as 0.50199997425079346 = float32(0.502), so a divergence living entirely below ~6e-8 m would be invisible here.  The refutation this rung exists to see is 9.152 m by 1000 steps, eight orders above that

checks.name: repeat_length
checks.why: |steps(a) - steps(b)|.  A run that ended early has a trivially small delta OVER THE OVERLAP, which is how a truncated replica passes a determinism check

checks.name: sensitivity_shortfall
checks.why: max(0, 1e-03 - max|a - c|), c being the same scene with the dropped cube's spawn x moved by 1e-06 m.  THE CONTROL: a frozen world is perfectly deterministic, so repeat_delta alone is not evidence.  One-sided (the roll_overrun idiom) and it needs no calibration -- float64 round-off over 2000 steps reaches ~1e-14 relative, ten orders short of this

checks.name: fall_interval
checks.why: rung 2's derivation, unchanged, on the dropped cube.  THE ANALYTIC ANCHOR: an engine that is deterministic and WRONG passes both determinism checks -- gravity at 5 m/s^2 is exactly as reproducible as 9.81 -- and this is the only check here that sees it

checks.name: distinct_processes
checks.why: the replicas must come from DISTINCT PROCESSES, asserted from the pid and process-start time each run records.  A determinism rung whose two replicas are one process -- or one array copied -- measures the arm.  This is the one place the ladder checks the arm rather than the engine, and it is cheap

rows.title: same pile twice, plus a 1 um sensitivity control

checks.name: distance_worst
checks.why: worst relative error, over every robot of every fleet size (1, 4, 8, 16), of d_i against omega_i r t -- the distance that robot would travel ALONE.  The tolerance is rung 4's and is NOT widened with N: the failure this rung exists to catch is a silently truncated constraint vector, documented at 9% displacement error, so a tolerance that grew with N would be pre-authorised to miss it

checks.name: wheel_omega_worst
checks.why: worst relative error of any robot's mean wheel rate against ITS OWN command.  The commands cycle, so an engine that simulates one robot and copies it lands every clone on one target and reds here

checks.name: roll_overrun_worst
checks.why: rung 4's one-sided kinematic invariant over the whole fleet and the whole run: no body may outrun its own wheels, at any N

checks.name: ride_worst
checks.why: worst axle deviation from floor_top + wheel_radius over every robot, every fleet and every sample after the initial settle

checks.name: lateral_worst
checks.why: worst |y - y_0| over every robot and every sample: each robot stays in its own lane at every fleet size

checks.name: separation_shortfall
checks.why: max over every fleet of max(0, 1.5 - min pairwise centre distance over the whole run).  All robots start abreast one lane apart and travel at different speeds, so they can only separate.  Asserted GEOMETRICALLY from the poses rather than as a contact count, because this tree has shipped a contact read that returned an empty set for a scene containing 1008 contacts

checks.name: robots_seen
checks.why: every robot of every fleet was found and measured.  An engine that silently DROPS robots otherwise reports a well-behaved smaller fleet, and every other number in this rung would look fine
